*Overview
When a Ladder season ends, the top 32 players are selected for the Conquest Tournament.
Players advance or are eliminated through the bracket until a champion is decided.
The top three players get rare equipment rewards.
*Match Rules
Each match is best of three, with three battles:
First Match: 2v2 battle
Second Match: 3v3 battle
Third Match: 5v5 battle
A character can't be deployed in more than one of the three battles.
*Preparation and Entering Battle
Preparation:
Before each match, players must set their battle lineup.
Entering battle:
1. When the battle enters its preparation phase, players wait on the Conquest Tournament screen.
2. Players in a non-safe zone can't take part.
3. Players who are teamed up or following someone can't take part.
4. 10 seconds before the battle starts, a ready screen pops up. Once ready, players are pulled into the arena in real time and fight manually.
*Victory Conditions
1. Defeat all of the opponent's deployed characters to win.
2. If the battle runs past the time limit, the side with more HP advances.
*Betting and Support
1. Players can bet on the champion before the Top 32 matches start.
2. A bet costs 100 Blue Diamonds.
3. If your pick wins the title, you get up to 2000 Blue Diamonds.
4. Before each match you can support your favorite player. If they advance, you receive a support reward.
*Champion Display
The top three players are shown on the Champion Display screen until the current tournament ends.
*Tournament Cycle
Each Conquest Tournament lasts one month
*Rewards
1. Every qualifier gets rare equipment and a title.
2. See the cycle on the Conquest Tournament screen for reward details.
3. A successful support grants 50 Arena Coins.
*The battle Support feature is disabled in the Conquest Tournament.

Gold is the only resource for buying characters, refreshing the shop and upgrading your ship in Island Conquest. You earn it automatically each wave, and selling characters refunds some Gold
The odds of drawing each quality change as your level rises

*Island Conquest is open daily 10:00~24:00
 
*Each match has 8 players.
 
Use your characters to fend off monsters and other players' attacks.
 
If your defense fails, you lose HP. When your HP hits zero, you're out.
 
The last player standing wins.
*You earn EXP and Gold during the match.
 
Enough EXP raises your level, increasing how many characters you can deploy and the odds of drawing high-quality ones.
 
Gold buys characters and EXP, or refreshes the Character Shop.
*Choosing the right characters is the key to victory.
 
All players draw from a shared character pool.
 
With 3 identical characters of the same star level, you can upgrade them into a stronger one.
 
Deploying several characters of a certain group or class activates extra bonuses.

*At the start of each round you get round Gold, win streak bonus Gold, loss streak compensation Gold and interest Gold.
 
You get 1 EXP at the start of each round.
 
The Character Shop refreshes automatically at the start of each round.
 
*During the preparation phase you can adjust your lineup and positions, or merge characters.
 
During preparation, characters on the board can temporarily exceed the deployment limit.
 
When preparation ends, characters over the limit are pulled back automatically; if the bench is full, the extras are sold automatically.
 
*In the battle phase, each player is randomly assigned an opponent to defend against.
 
Each player is the opponent of only 1 player per battle phase.
 
You can't adjust characters on the board during the battle phase.
 
In waves 1, 2 and 3 you defend against preset NPCs.
 
*If your defense fails, you take damage based on the number and stars of the opponent's remaining characters. When your warship's HP hits 0, you're out.

*Each match starts with a Lv1 warship. Earn enough warship EXP to level it up.
 
You get 1 warship EXP automatically at the start of each round.
 
Spend 5 Gold on Build Warship to gain 4 warship EXP instantly.
 
*Warship level sets the maximum number of deployable characters
 
Warship level sets the odds of each character quality appearing in the Character Shop.

*Round Gold: at the start of each round, get Gold based on the current round number.
 
Win Streak Bonus / Loss Streak Compensation: at the start of each round, get Gold based on your current win or loss streak.
 
Interest Gold: at the start of each round, get 10% interest on the Gold you hold, up to 5 Gold per round.
 
Victory Reward: at the start of each round, get 2 Gold if you won the previous battle.
 
Sell Characters: selling characters you own returns some Gold.
 
*Buy Characters: spend Gold in the Character Shop to buy characters. The shop refreshes automatically at the start of each round.
 
Refresh: spend 2 Gold to refresh the Character Shop instantly
 
Build Warship: spend 5 Gold to gain 4 EXP instantly.

*Deploy 3 identical characters to raise their star level.
 
Higher-star characters are stronger
 
Each character can reach up to 3 stars
 
*Every character belongs to a specific group and class
 
Deploying enough different characters of one group or class activates its bonus.
 
Bonuses with different count requirements can stack.

*Buy characters in the Character Shop.
 
All characters in the Character Shop are 1-star.
 
When a player is eliminated, their shop characters return to the pool.
 
*The Character Shop refreshes automatically at the start of each round.
 
Use Refresh at any phase to refresh the Character Shop for 2 Gold.
 
When the shop refreshes, the odds of each quality appearing depend on warship level.
 
*While locked, the Character Shop won't refresh at the start of a round.
 
Refreshing while locked removes the lock.
 
The shop lock lasts only 1 round.

*Dear Captain, the new Masters Tournament opens on 3/30. Reach the top 80 of the Ladder Peak Arena to qualify (selection uses the leaderboard when the Ladder Peak Arena ends on 3/29). Keep an eye on the Masters Tournament schedule and your qualification status.

*Availability: the Masters Tournament is an event mode based on the Ladder Peak Arena and is not permanent.
This Masters Tournament selects captains from the leaderboard when the Ladder Peak Arena ends on 3/29.
Captains in the top 80 of each war zone's leaderboard (expanded this season) qualify for the Masters Tournament (servers open for less than a set time are excluded from selection)*Qualified captains are placed in one of three divisions by server: East Blue/West Blue/South Blue/North Blue/New World/Supernova captains form one division, Zou captains form another, and Skypiea captains form the third.*Once qualified, captains must set up a separate lineup.
The Masters Tournament isn't open all day, only 11:00-13:00 and 19:00-21:00 daily.
Battles and scoring work much like the Ladder Peak Arena.
The Masters Tournament lasts three weeks. When it ends, captains receive titles and other rewards based on their rank.
Captains who play 10 or more Masters matches per week earn Masters Gold based on their points. Use Masters Gold to buy valuable items in the Arena Shop.

uncertain_notes: Captain's Guide: game_terms_v271 gives 大航海 = 'Grand Voyage', but the earlier batches and the item 大航海挂机次数券 use 'Great Voyage'; 'Great Voyage' was kept (e.g. 大航海商店 = 'Great Voyage Shop').

Captain's Guide: 角色突破 kept as the in-game 'Hero Break' and 角色升级 as the in-game 'Character Level Up', even though the two use different nouns.

TableNewStrongGuideTarget row 18 (primary bundle): label 晶魂商城 (Crystal Soul Shop) but the text says 'from the Arena Shop' (天梯商店); translated as written. Row 15: label 讨伐任务 (Bounty Quest) but text mentions Blood Battle; translated as written. Row 37 (other bundle): label 黄金试炼 (Golden Trial) but text mentions Hero Trial; translated as written.
Character names in guide labels follow game_terms_v271 exactly (大熊 = 'Bartholomew Kuma', 艾斯 = 'Portgas D. Ace', 莫利亚 = 'Gecko Moria', 汉库珂 = 'Boa Hancock', 杰克斯 = 'Shanks').

TableAutoChessGroup: game_terms gives 自然之力 = 'Force of Nature'; the two sibling bonds were rendered in the same spirit: 动物之力 = 'Animal Force', 超人之力 = 'Superhuman Force' (they are the Zoan / Paramecia bonds; the buff texts use Zoans/Logias).
TableAutoChessGrade: 罗刹 rendered 'Rakshasa' (the demon it names); 名人 rendered 'Master'. Tier names are 'Novice/Expert/Master/Rakshasa' + rank number, and the top tier 至高 = 'Supreme'.
TableAutoChessHeroRare: 普通/优秀/精良/史诗/传说 rendered as the usual rarity scale Common/Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary (game_terms has 普通 = 'Normal', but that comes from a difficulty/quality context).

TableText ChessRewardEndDesc: source 'M月d日 HH:mm结算' looks like a .NET DateTime format string, so the English word is quoted as a format literal: "'Ends' M/d HH:mm". If the game does not use it as a DateTime format, the quotes would show; drop them then.
TableText AutoChess_Level_N '{0}段' rendered 'Rank {0}'. If the game prefixes it with the tier name (e.g. 初心 + '{0}段'), a leading space may be needed locally ('Novice' + ' Rank 9').
TableText ACExplainPageWikiSubPageRoundTabContent: the source's '获得会和金币' is a typo for 回合金币 ('round Gold') and was translated that way.
TableText ACExplainPageWikiSubPageHeroTabContent says bonuses of different counts stack, while TableAutoChessGroup.desc says only the highest tier triggers; both translated as written.

TableText: 助战 (the battle Support/assist feature) vs 支持 (supporting a player in the tournament bets) are both 'Support' in English; the LadderWar_Rule line about 助战 was written 'The battle Support feature is disabled' to keep them apart.

ui_texts: developer placeholder texts (玩家名玩家名, 描述描述…, 蚊子蚊子…, 文本内容…, 水电费…, 杰拉基尔, 木给瓦拉撸费, 面子果实) were translated literally but kept short; they are overwritten at runtime. 木给瓦拉撸费 is a joke transliteration of 'Mugiwara Luffy'.
ui_texts: '周六24点结算' uses the in-game rendering 'Settles Saturday at hour 24' from game_terms_v271.
TableItem: the name column was already English in both bundles and is copied verbatim (including its existing irregular spacing such as 'Sabo ( Halloween Outfit )'). Only intro was translated.

TableItem: item, outfit, title and character names inside the descriptions use game_terms_v271 or, preferably, the English name of the matching TableItem row (outfit names come from the matching outfit-unlock items). Where the two disagree, the TableItem name was kept because the player sees it on the item itself: 英雄·暴走… = 'Hero Rampage…' (game_terms has 'Frenzy'), 艾斯的皮艇 = 'Ace's Dinghy' (game_terms: 'Ace's Striker'), 恶意狼号 = 'Wicked Wolf' (game_terms: 'Grudge Dolph'), 可爱小鸭号 = 'Lovely Duck' (game_terms: 'Cute Duck'), 推进城汉库珂 = 'Impel Down Boa Hancock'.

TableItem: Chinese number units were converted into full English numbers, so a few digit strings differ from the source while the values stay the same: 10亿 = 1 billion, 10万 = 100,000, 5万 = 50,000, 50w = 500,000, 25W = 250,000 … 750W = 7,500,000, 1W = 10,000, 1.5W = 15,000.
TableItem: 破击 is 'Block Break' in item texts (matching the item 'Advanced Block Break Elixir'); 闪避 is 'Evasion' (the item itself is named 'Advanced Dodge Elixir').

TableItem: some titles share the same English in the installed game (挥金如土 and 一掷千金 both 'Money to Burn'; 海域先锋 and 海域尖兵 both 'Sea Vanguard'; 航海强者 'Sea Veteran'). Kept as the item names show them; 海域精锐, which has no item, was rendered 'Sea Elite'.
TableItem 225003 'Cute Apple': the skill name 雷普 is crude internet slang; it was transliterated as 'Leipu' rather than translated.

TableItem: obvious source typos were translated by intent (和之国乔巴（乔巴门卫） = Chopaemon, AppIeID = Apple ID, 布玲飞毯） = Charlotte Pudding (Flying Carpet), 和之国山治/索隆/娜美 = Wano Sanji/Zoro/Nami). 520187's list contains an empty entry (',,') in the source, kept as ', ,'. 619160 '测试' = 'Test'.
